end

def asc_token!
  require "spaceship"
  Spaceship::ConnectAPI.token ||= Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Token.create(
    key_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID"],
    issuer_id: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID"],
    key: ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"]
  )
end

def asc_app!(bundle_id:)
  require "spaceship"
  app = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::App.find(bundle_id)
  UI.user_error!("App #{bundle_id} not found in App Store Connect") if app.nil?
  app
end

# E3: pilot resolves groups BY NAME and silently skips adding the build when
# the name resolves to nothing — fail loudly instead, pointing at the
# variable. Returns [app, matched_group].
def find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id:, group:)
  asc_token!
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  found = app.get_beta_groups(includes: nil, limit: 200).select { |g| g.name == group }
  UI.user_error!("TestFlight external group '#{group}' (TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP) not found in App Store Connect — create it or fix the repo variable. Nothing was uploaded.") if found.empty?
  [app, found.first]
end

# gh-1041 (AC1): appearance is NO LONGER the submit leg's job — ASC
# read-side lag (group membership trailing an already-successful
# distribution, #855: run 36382214186 died in a 900s wait-loop while the
# build was in fact live) must never fail a green `upload_to_testflight`.
# After a successful upload ONE read-only probe runs, purely informational
# and unable to raise: found → ✅ line; not yet → a note pointing at the
# deferred store-appearance-check workflow, which re-checks the store
# 120 min after the legs start and files/updates exactly one stub if the
# version is still absent past the horizon. Leg success = upload success.
def verify_external_distribution!(bundle_id:, group:, app_version:)
  probe = lambda do
    app, beta_group = find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id: bundle_id, group: group)
    group_build_ids = beta_group.fetch_builds.map(&:id)
    build = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Build.all(
      app_id: app.id,
      includes: "preReleaseVersion,buildBetaDetail",
      processing_states: "VALID",
      sort: "-uploadedDate",
      limit: 100
    ).select { |b| b.app_version == app_version && group_build_ids.include?(b.id) }
     .max_by { |b| b.version.to_i }
    if build
      # fastlane deleted BuildBetaDetail#ready_for_external_testing? but left
      # Build#ready_for_external_testing? calling it — NoMethodError the
      # moment ASC returns buildBetaDetail (issue #362; green runs only saw
      # nil, which short-circuits). Read external_build_state from the beta
      # detail directly: IN_BETA_TESTING/BETA_APPROVED = live, anything else
      # (incl. nil detail) = still waiting for Beta App Review.
      external_state = build.build_beta_detail&.external_build_state
      if external_state == "IN_BETA_TESTING" || external_state == "BETA_APPROVED"
        UI.success("✅ #{app_version} (build #{build.version}) is live to the external group '#{group}' — distributed with zero clicks")
      else
        UI.important("Build #{app_version} (#{build.version}) is in '#{group}' and waiting for Beta App Review — external visibility flips automatically on approval, no clicks needed.")
      end
    else
      UI.important("Build #{app_version} not visible in '#{group}' yet — the submit stays GREEN (gh-1041: store read-side lag is not a failure). The deferred store-appearance-check workflow re-checks ASC 120 min after the daily legs start and files/updates one stub if the version is still absent past the horizon.")
    end
  end
  begin
    probe.call
  rescue StandardError => e
    UI.important("Post-submit appearance probe skipped (#{e.class}: #{e.message.to_s[0, 160]}) — the upload above already succeeded; the deferred store-appearance-check workflow owns appearance verification (gh-1041, #855).")
  end
end

# Read-only ASC facts for one platform → AppstorePreflight decision (AC3:
# every check happens BEFORE any mutation).
def appstore_submission_decision(bundle_id:, platform:, version:, confirm:)
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  # gh-1519 read-side: a version freshly created by store-metadata.yml can
  # trail in ASC reads — bounded retry (3 × 20s) instead of an instant
  # fail, covering BOTH arms like the macOS app_store lane's preflight
  # probe: a nil find (read lag) AND a raised call (transient ASC 500).
  # The retry decision lives in AppstorePreflight so the matrix is
  # plain-ruby testable (test/appstore_preflight_test.rb).
  app_store_version = AppstorePreflight.with_visibility_retries(
    attempts: 3,
    delay: 20,
    log: ->(msg) { UI.important(msg) },
    sleep_fn: ->(secs) { sleep(secs) }
  ) do
    app
      .get_app_store_versions(filter: { platform: platform })
      .find { |v| v.version_string == version }
  end
  builds = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Build.all(
    app_id: app.id,
    version: version,
    platform: platform,
    processing_states: "PROCESSING,VALID,FAILED,INVALID"
  )
  decision = AppstorePreflight.decide(
    version: version,
    confirm: confirm,
    app_store_version: app_store_version && { "state" => app_store_version.app_store_state },
    builds: builds.map { |b| { "number" => b.version, "state" => b.processing_state } }
  )
  [app, decision]
end

def store_summary_line(line)
  path = ENV["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"]
  File.write(path, "#{line}\n", mode: "a") if path
  UI.success(line)
end

# Builds a temp metadata dir for deliver from fastlane/metadata/<platform_key>/
# with App Store locale names, release_notes.txt from the store_artefacts
# changelogs (en fallback per locale), and WITHOUT name.txt/subtitle.txt —
# App Info is not editable once the app is released, and deliver would fail.
def build_store_metadata_dir(platform_key:, out_dir:)
  FileUtils.rm_rf(out_dir)
  FileUtils.mkdir_p(out_dir)
  store_locale_map.each do |src_locale, as_locale|
    src = "metadata/#{platform_key}/#{src_locale}"
    FileUtils.cp_r(src, "#{out_dir}/#{as_locale}") if Dir.exist?(src)
  end
  en_notes = store_latest_changelog("en")
  ru_notes = store_latest_changelog("ru")
  store_locale_map.each_value do |as_locale|
    dir = "#{out_dir}/#{as_locale}"
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(dir)
    notes = as_locale == "ru" && !ru_notes.empty? ? ru_notes : en_notes
    File.write("#{dir}/release_notes.txt", notes)
    FileUtils.rm_f("#{dir}/name.txt")
    FileUtils.rm_f("#{dir}/subtitle.txt")
  end
end

# Copies committed store goldens (flutter_app/test/goldens/store/<lang>/<device>)
# into the deliver screenshots folder with App Store locale names, falling
# back to English when a locale has no localized screenshots.
def copy_store_screenshots(device:, suffix:, out_root:)
  goldens = File.expand_path("../test/goldens/store", __dir__)
  store_locale_map.each do |src_locale, as_locale|
    lang = src_locale.split("-").first.downcase
    dir = "#{out_root}/#{as_locale}"
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(dir)
    files = Dir.glob("#{goldens}/#{lang}/#{device}/*.png").sort.first(10)
    if files.empty?
      files = Dir.glob("#{goldens}/en/#{device}/*.png").sort.first(10)
      UI.message("No #{device} screenshots for #{as_locale}, using en fallback") unless files.empty?
    end
    files.each do |f|
      FileUtils.cp(f, "#{dir}/#{File.basename(f, ".*")}#{suffix}.png")
    end
  end
end

# Apple's Connect API 500s in bursts (even seconds apart on identical
# requests) — retry the block a few times on "Server error got 500".
def with_apple_retries(attempts: 3, delay: 25)
  tries = 0
  begin
    tries += 1
    yield
  rescue => e
    if e.message.include?("Server error got 500") && tries < attempts
      UI.important("Apple API 500 (attempt #{tries}/#{attempts}) — retrying in #{delay}s...")
      sleep(delay)
      retry
    end
    raise
  end
end

# gh-1519: store-metadata's app_store lanes must CREATE the App Store
# version when absent — deliver runs with skip_app_version_update:true,
# which never materializes the record, so release-appstore.yml's
# pre-flight dead-ended on every fresh version (v1.0.548 needed a manual
# ASC click). Idempotent: POSTs appStoreVersions only when the version is
# missing, so re-running store-metadata on an existing version stays a
# metadata-only update (no duplicate version error).
def ensure_app_store_version!(bundle_id:, platform:, version:)
  asc_token!
  app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
  existing = with_apple_retries(attempts: 3, delay: 20) do
    app.get_app_store_versions(filter: { platform: platform }).map(&:version_string)
  end
  return app unless StoreVersionCreate.needs_create?(existing: existing, version: version)

  UI.message("App Store version #{version} (#{platform}) does not exist yet — creating the version record before deliver (gh-1519)")
  begin
    # Reuse an editable version (PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION / REJECTED / ...)
    # when one exists: Apple rejects a second version in that state. With
    # no editable version this performs the same appStoreVersions POST.
    app.ensure_version!(version, platform: platform)
  rescue => e
    # gh-1519 rework (review thread, PR #1520): ASC read lag can hide a
    # version a PREVIOUS run created, so needs_create? above answers true
    # and the POST collides with the existing record — on a workflow
    # re-run that conflict is idempotency, not failure (the ticket's REG:
    # re-running store-metadata on an existing version stays a
    # metadata-only update). Re-read once (bounded retries) and no-op
    # when the version now exists; anything else still raises.
    if StoreVersionCreate.create_conflict?(message: e.message)
      UI.important("ensure_version! reports #{version} (#{platform}) already exists — re-reading once to confirm (ASC read lag)")
      existing = with_apple_retries(attempts: 3, delay: 20) do
        app.get_app_store_versions(filter: { platform: platform }).map(&:version_string)
      end
      return app unless StoreVersionCreate.needs_create?(existing: existing, version: version)
    end
    raise
  end
  UI.success("Synchronized App Store version #{version} (#{platform}) — store-metadata can now attach metadata/screenshots to it")
  app
end

# Directly updates App Store version localizations via the Spaceship API.
# Fallback when deliver fails because App Info is not editable.
def upload_version_metadata_via_api(metadata_dir:, bundle_id:, platform:)
  require "spaceship"

  app = Spaceship::ConnectAPI::App.find(bundle_id)
  if app.nil?
    UI.error("Could not find app with bundle_id: #{bundle_id}")
    return
  end

  version = app.get_edit_app_store_version(platform: platform)
  if version.nil?
    UI.important("No editable version found for #{bundle_id} on #{platform} - skipping")
    return
  end

  locs = version.get_app_store_version_localizations
  updated = 0
  locs.each do |loc|
    locale_dir = File.join(metadata_dir, loc.locale)
    attrs = {}
    {
      "release_notes"    => :whatsNew,
      "description"      => :description,
      "keywords"         => :keywords,
      "promotional_text" => :promotionalText
    }.each do |file_name, attr_key|
      file_path = File.join(locale_dir, "#{file_name}.txt")
      attrs[attr_key] = File.read(file_path).strip if File.exist?(file_path)
    end
    unless attrs.empty?
      loc.update(attributes: attrs)
      updated += 1
    end
  end
  UI.success("Updated #{updated} locale(s) version metadata via Spaceship API")
end

platform :ios do
  # gh-798 AC1/AC2: the daily TestFlight leg asserts the version it is
  # about to stamp is strictly ABOVE the latest ASC-approved version BEFORE
  # any build runs — #785's failure class (altool 90062 at the end of a
  # 20-minute build) dies here in seconds instead. Reads the SAME version
  # source the build stamps (BUILD_NAME — pubspec → tag → version job, the
  # one-version scheme gh-785 centralized). The decision lives in
  # version_floor.rb (plain-ruby tested); this lane only fetches ASC facts.
  desc "Assert the stamped version is above the ASC-approved floor before building (gh-798)"
  lane :assert_version_floor do
    stamped = ENV["BUILD_NAME"].to_s.strip
    UI.user_error!("[gh-798] BUILD_NAME is not set — the version-floor pre-check needs the version the build will stamp") if stamped.empty?

    if ENV["APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT"].to_s.strip.empty?
      # ASC keys are optional repo secrets: without them the submit leg
      # skips the upload anyway, so there is no floor to guard. The skip
      # stays a visible marker, never a silent pass (gh-798 AC4).
      UI.important("[gh-798] version-floor pre-check: SKIPPED — no APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT secret (the upload leg would skip too)")
      next
    end

    bundle_id = ENV["IOS_BUNDLE_ID"] || "dev.fa1.app"
    # E1: ASC unreachable/rate-limited gets exactly one retry, then a
    # fail-closed named error — a skipped floor check is a silent floor.
    tries = 0
    begin
      tries += 1
      asc_token!
      app = asc_app!(bundle_id: bundle_id)
      approved = app.get_app_store_versions(filter: { platform: Spaceship::ConnectAPI::Platform::IOS }).map do |v|
        { "state" => v.app_store_state, "version" => v.version_string }
      end
    rescue FastlaneCore::Interface::FastlaneError
      # gh-800 r2: deterministic lane errors (missing ASC app, missing
      # TestFlight group, any UI.user_error!) are NOT transient — re-raise
      # immediately instead of retrying them and mislabeling the failure
      # "App Store Connect unreachable".
      raise
    rescue StandardError => e
      retry if tries < 2
      UI.user_error!("[gh-798] version-floor pre-check: App Store Connect unreachable after one retry (#{e.class}: #{e.message.to_s[0, 200]}) — failing closed: cannot verify the version floor, refusing to build")
    end

    decision = VersionFloor.decide(stamped: stamped, approved: approved)
    # AC4 leg-level marker: the pre-check RAN and what it decided — visible
    # in the daily report, so a silently-skipped check can never hide.
    UI.message("[gh-798] version-floor pre-check RAN: stamped=#{stamped} approved_floor=#{decision['floor']} verdict=#{decision['action']}")
    UI.user_error!(decision["reason"]) if decision["action"] == "abort"
    UI.success("✅ #{decision['reason']}")
  end

  desc "Build iOS IPA only (for CI split build/submit pattern)"
  lane :build_only do
    # gh-1865 model v3: the signing identity lives in the PERSISTENT host
    # keychain (ci-signing.keychain-db), provisioned by the workflow via
    # ~/bin/ci-sign. No per-job keychain, no search-list writes here (the
    # additive-helper dance retired with per-job keychains — gh-1866/
    # gh-1865). Point-of-use unlock right before the archive: hours can
    # pass between the workflow's provision step and gym, and an explicit
    # unlock is immune to any gap length (the gh-1798 auto-lock window
    # hack is retired). gh-1910 lesson kept: resolve the script absolutely
    # from the Fastfile location (__dir__ = flutter_app/fastlane →
    # repo/scripts) — fastlane's sh does not honor the assumed lane cwd.
    ci_sign = File.expand_path("../../scripts/ci-sign", __dir__)
    sh(ci_sign, "unlock")
    lane_start = Time.now

    team_id = ENV["IOS_TEAM_ID"] || "YP9HC3USZ3"
    bundle_id = ENV["IOS_BUNDLE_ID"] || "dev.fa1.app"
    profile_name = ENV["IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_NAME"] || "Fa Profile"
    live_activity_profile_name = ENV["IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_NAME"] || "FaLiveActivity Profile"
    # gh-1865: CI passes a SHA-1 fingerprint (IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY read
    # from the job's own keychain right after import) — never resolve the
    # identity by NAME, which is a lottery when the additive per-user
    # search list holds two same-CN "Apple Distribution" certs from
    # concurrent signing legs. The bare name below is a LOCAL-dev fallback
    # only; the workflow always pins.
    signing_identity = ENV["IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY"] || "iPhone Distribution"

    update_code_signing_settings(
      use_automatic_signing: false,
      path: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj",
      team_id: team_id,
      bundle_identifier: bundle_id,
      profile_name: profile_name,
      code_sign_identity: signing_identity,
      # ONLY the app target: without this filter the action rewrites EVERY
      # target's PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER (incl. the FaLiveActivity
      # extension), producing a CFBundleIdentifier collision at upload.
      targets: ["Runner"]
    )

    # The FaLiveActivity extension signs MANUALLY as well: the runner's Xcode
    # has no Apple account, so automatic signing / -allowProvisioningUpdates
    # cannot create its profile — it is installed from a secret by the
    # workflow and only gets pointed at here.
    update_code_signing_settings(
      use_automatic_signing: false,
      path: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj",
      team_id: team_id,
      bundle_identifier: "#{bundle_id}.FaLiveActivity",
      profile_name: live_activity_profile_name,
      code_sign_identity: signing_identity,
      targets: ["FaLiveActivity"]
    )

    sh("flutter", "clean")
    sh("flutter", "pub", "get")
    cocoapods(podfile: "ios/Podfile")

    if ENV["BUILD_NUMBER"]
      increment_build_number(xcodeproj: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj", build_number: ENV["BUILD_NUMBER"])
    else
      increment_build_number(xcodeproj: "ios/Runner.xcodeproj")
    end

    # Issue #726 (run 35564638018): ASC closes a version train once a build
    # of it was approved (90186) and rejects submissions not higher than the
    # previously approved version (90062) — with pubspec pinned at 1.0.0 the
    # daily TestFlight upload can never land again. BUILD_NAME comes from
    # build-mobile.yml (the derived next-tag version, strictly increasing);
    # unset = legacy manual flow, keep the pubspec version.
    build_name_args = ENV["BUILD_NAME"] ? ["--build-name", ENV["BUILD_NAME"]] : []
    sh("xcrun simctl list > /dev/null 2>&1 || true")
    sh("xcrun simctl boot 'iPhone 16' 2>/dev/null || xcrun simctl boot 'iPhone 15' 2>/dev/null || true")
    sh("flutter", "build", "ios", "--release", "--no-codesign", *build_name_args)

    # gh-1954: point-of-use re-unlock right before gym — the lane-start
    # unlock goes stale during the long CocoaPods/SPM phase, and gym's
    # `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings` hangs on a locked keychain's GUI
    # prompt (headless = fastlane timeout, run 40849468765).
    sh(ci_sign, "unlock")

    # gh-1954: keychain re-unlock WATCHDOG for the whole gym window. The
    # keychain auto-locks after ~5 min of inactivity and
    # set-keychain-settings can never fix it non-interactively on this
    # host (GUI SecurityAgent prompt — screenshot-confirmed). A locked
    # keychain mid-archive/export = xcodebuild hangs on the password
    # prompt. unlock-keychain -p never prompts, so re-unlocking every
    # 60 s keeps the signing identity usable through archive AND export.
    unlock_watchdog = Thread.new do
      loop do
        sleep 60
        begin
          sh(ci_sign, "unlock")
        rescue StandardError
          # best effort — a transient unlock failure must not kill the build
        end
      end
    end

    # gh-1954: xcodebuild resolves signing identities ONLY through the
    # user keychain search list — and on the shared host a concurrent
    # signing leg rewrites that list mid-build (run 40843155381: doctor OK
    # at 08:38, then gym at 08:53 resolved a same-team "Apple Distribution"
    # from a DIFFERENT keychain instead of the pinned 9007ED87 from
    # ci-signing.keychain-db — profile/cert mismatch). Pin the search list
    # for the duration of gym and restore it in ensure. This is NOT the
    # retired per-job keychain model: the keychain itself stays persistent;
    # only xcodebuild's visibility window is pinned.
    # gh-1972 root cause: the save/restore dance entrenched whatever it
    # captured — one System duplicate slipping in between the two writers
    # (this pin + ci-sign install append) was then written back by EVERY
    # subsequent run, and a later "Reset To Defaults" on the host turned
    # the stale login path dangling ("Keychain Not Found" GUI dialogs,
    # gh auth failure). The pin below IS the canonical persistent list;
    # there is nothing to restore to.
    sh("security", "list-keychains", "-d", "user", "-s",
       File.expand_path("~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"),
       "/Library/Keychains/System.keychain",
       File.expand_path("~/Library/Keychains/ci-signing.keychain-db"))

    # gh-1692: xcbeautify, never xcpretty (xcpretty swallowed the archive
    # error — silent `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`), and on failure the newest
    # gym log tail lands in the job log via print_gym_log_tail.
    begin
      build_app(
        workspace: "ios/Runner.xcworkspace",
        scheme: "Runner",
        export_method: "app-store",
        output_directory: "build/ios/ipa",
        output_name: "fa.ipa",
        skip_build_archive: false,
        clean: true,
        sdk: "iphoneos",
        xcodebuild_formatter: "xcbeautify",
        export_options: {
          method: "app-store",
          provisioningProfiles: {
            bundle_id => profile_name,
            "#{bundle_id}.FaLiveActivity" => live_activity_profile_name
          },
          signingStyle: "manual",
          # gh-1865: pin the export step by the same fingerprint — the
          # exportOptions signingCertificate accepts a SHA-1 (that is what
          # Xcode itself writes into exportOptions plists), so
          # -exportArchive cannot resolve a shadowing same-CN cert either.
          signingCertificate: signing_identity,
          teamID: team_id,
          manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber: false,
          uploadBitcode: false,
          compileBitcode: false
        },
        export_xcargs: "-allowProvisioningUpdates"
      )
    rescue StandardError => e
      print_gym_log_tail(since: lane_start)
      raise e
    ensure
      unlock_watchdog.kill
      # gh-1954: restore the pre-gym search list (best effort — never mask
      # the gym result with a restore failure).
      begin
        # gh-1972: no write-back restore. The pinned list is canonical and
        # idempotent — restoring a captured copy only re-entrenches any
        # garbage captured at pin time (see the root-cause note above).
      rescue StandardError
      end
    end
  end

  desc "Upload the built IPA to TestFlight and distribute to the external group (no metadata/screenshots)"
  lane :submit_only do
    ipa = ENV["IOS_IPA_PATH"] || File.expand_path("../build/ios/ipa/fa.ipa", __dir__)
    UI.user_error!("IPA not found: #{ipa} (set IOS_IPA_PATH)") unless File.exist?(ipa)

    # Loud named failures at lane start (AC1) — a missing variable must
    # never surface as a fastlane stack trace after the upload.
    group = external_testflight_group!
    review_info = beta_app_review_info!
    feedback_email = beta_app_feedback_email!
    bundle_id = ENV["IOS_BUNDLE_ID"] || "dev.fa1.app"
    find_external_testflight_group!(bundle_id: bundle_id, group: group)

    upload_to_testflight(
      api_key: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value],
      ipa: ipa,
      # External distribution needs a PROCESSED build: skipping the wait
      # makes pilot silently skip distribution (bounded, E1).
      skip_waiting_for_build_processing: false,
      wait_processing_timeout_duration: testflight_wait_timeout,
      distribute_external: true,
      groups: [group],
      notify_external_testers: true,
      changelog: testflight_changelog,
      beta_app_review_info: review_info,
      beta_app_feedback_email: feedback_email,
      uses_non_exempt_encryption: false
    )

    # Select the uploaded build by the marketing version it actually ships
    # (BUILD_NAME when the build lane set it, issue #726; pubspec otherwise).
    verify_external_distribution!(bundle_id: bundle_id, group: group, app_version: ENV["BUILD_NAME"] || store_pubspec_version)

content.text:
# maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --coverage=coverage

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2125 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily TestFlight leg's "Build iOS IPA" job (build-mobile run 43160591145, step 19) died 12 minutes into the fastlane gym archive with exit 65 — `SwiftCompile normal arm64` failed on missing/inaccessible build state.

**Root cause**: `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` → `build_only` lane → `build_app(...)` ran with **no `derived_data_path` and no `archive_path`**, so `xcodebuild archive` fell back to the **default per-user, path-hashed DerivedData** (`~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-ecmkpbjauzuoejdrlckdeqdusmvi`) and the default per-user archive dir (`~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives/<date>/`). On this persistent self-hosted Mac:

- nothing in the pipeline ever cleans that directory — the lane's `flutter clean` removes only `flutter_app/build/`, and gym's `clean: true` cleans *through* the very `XCBuildData/build.db` that corrupted (verified: the failing log's archive command carries no `-derivedDataPath`, and the repo contains zero references to DerivedData cleanup);
- the Mac serves up to three concurrent runner registrations under the same user (documented in the Fastfile gh-2026 note), all sharing that per-user root — including `SDKExplicitPrecompiledModules`, which every build's `PruneExplicitPrecompiledModules` step prunes while siblings may be reading it;
- months of daily archives from different commits accumulated stale incremental state there.

The corruption surfaced as the trio in the log: `unable to read PCH file .../Runner-primary-Bridging-header.pch: No such file or directory`, `cannot open constant extraction protocol list input file .../Runner_const_extract_protocols.json`, and `accessing build database .../XCBuildData/build.db: disk I/O error` — the canonical stale/corupted-DerivedData signature (missing mid-build inputs + SQLite I/O failure on the xcbuild database).

**Impact**: Any daily/weekly TestFlight leg can red nondeterministically depending on which runner registration (fa-m5-1/2/3) picks the job and what state its shared DerivedData holds — run 43160591145 failed on commit `23e7396` while the **same tree built green the two previous days** (runs of 11-10 and 11-11), and the only intervening commit (gh-2120) touches unrelated release toolchains. Each red costs a full TestFlight day (submit-ios is gated on build-ios success).

**Fix approach**: Isolate, don't share. The `build_only` lane now pins a **workspace-local, per-run build state directory** — `build/ios/archive-dd` inside `flutter_app/build/` — passed to gym as `derived_data_path`, with the xcarchive pinned next to it (`archive_path`), and `FileUtils.rm_rf` removes the directory before the archive (covers hand-run lanes that skip `flutter clean`). The gh-160 checkout wipes and re-clones the workspace every run, so the directory starts clean by construction. Isolation is chosen over a shared-root purge deliberately: a blanket `rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData` would clobber a sibling registration's live archive (guarded against in the test).

**Previous attempt**: None — first failure of this class (no prior DerivedData/PCH/disk-I/O failures in the tracker's daily-publish history).

**Evidence**:
- Job log (`gh run view --job 130991132400`): archive ran 05:56→06:08 UTC, then the three error lines above, `(3 failures)`, `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`, exit status 65; build environment `gym 2.241.2`, `iPhoneOS27.1.sdk`, runner `fa-m5-2`.
- Archive invocation in the same log: `xcodebuild -workspace ios/Runner.xcworkspace ... -archivePath /Users/uladzimir_klyshevich/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives/2026-11-12/fa.xcarchive` — no `-derivedDataPath` present.
- `grep -rn DerivedData` over the repo (workflows, scripts, fastlane, docs): no cleanup or pinning anywhere before this fix.
- `gh run list -w build-mobile.yml`: 11-10 `success`, 11-11 `success`, 11-12 `failure` on the only-different-by-gh-2120 tree.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause
The TestFlight leg's gym archive ran with no `-derivedDataPath`/`archive_path`, so xcodebuild built into the **default per-user Xcode DerivedData** (`~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-<hash>`) on the persistent self-hosted Mac. Nothing in the pipeline ever cleans that directory (the lane's `flutter clean` touches only `flutter_app/build/`; gym's `clean: true` cleans through the very `build.db` that corrupted), and up to three concurrent runner registrations share it (gh-2026). Run 43160591145 died 12 minutes in on the classic corrupted-state trio — missing bridging PCH, missing `Runner_const_extract_protocols.json`, `build.db: disk I/O error` — while the **same tree built green the two previous days** (only delta was gh-2120, unrelated).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` (`ios build_only`): pin a workspace-local per-run build state dir (`build/ios/archive-dd`) as gym `derived_data_path`, pin `archive_path` next to it (the old default `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives/<date>/fa.xcarchive` is another shared same-day-collision surface), and `FileUtils.rm_rf` it before the archive. The gh-160 checkout re-clones the workspace every run, so the path starts clean by construction.
- Isolation over purge: the lane deliberately does NOT `rm -rf` the shared per-user DerivedData root — a sibling registration's archive may be live inside it (negative checks pin this).

### Test Coverage
- `test/workflow_ios_derived_data_guard_test.dart` — new workflow-shape guard (gh-1692 pattern), written first and RED against the old lane: AC1 workspace-local `derived_data_path`, AC2 removal before the archive, AC3 workspace-local `archive_path`, AC4 negative — never purge the shared root from the Fastfile or from a build-ios step. **5/5 PASSED** after the fix.
- Sibling guards unaffected: `workflow_ios_archive_observability_test.dart`, `workflow_ios_platform_download_guard_test.dart`, `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart`, `release_ipa_strip_test.dart` — 29 tests PASSED; all 8 `flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb` PASSED; `ruby -c Fastfile` OK.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (CI per-PR shape) — PASSED (see job log for counts).

### Notes
- Legacy `Runner-*` DerivedData dirs remain on fa-m5-1/2/3 and are now dead weight; owner may reclaim disk (a suspected contributing factor to the I/O error) via `rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData` **only while no iOS/macOS build is running on any registration** — the repo must not do it (concurrent-archives hazard).
- Fresh derived data makes each archive slightly slower than the (corruption-prone) incremental reuse; gym already ran `clean: true` per archive, so the delta is module/PCH caches only.
- The macOS desktop lane (`build-macos.yml`) shares the per-user DerivedData root and may hit the same class eventually — out of scope for this ticket (testflight leg), flagged for a follow-up.

input_completeness_preflight.md # ⚠️ STEP 0 — INPUT COMPLETENESS PRE-FLIGHT (surface scan, before ANY work) Right after reading the input files, run a QUICK (surface-level) go/no-go scan of the ticket — title, description, and comments authored by humans. — simplest possible change

— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## tdd_test_directory.md # TDD Test Directory Rules Write failing unit tests in the repository's existing unit-test tree **only**: - Discover the unit-test directory from the existing build and test configuration and from nearby tests for the code being changed. - Follow the naming, layout, and test-runner conventions already established in that directory. ❌ **Never** place development TDD tests under `testing/`. `testing/` is owned by test-automation agents (regression probes, workflow observation tests, accessibility gates, etc.). arguments.content:
### Root Cause
- The TestFlight leg's gym archive ran with no `derived_data_path`/`archive_path`, so xcodebuild built into the **default per-user Xcode DerivedData** (`~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-<hash>`) on the persistent self-hosted Mac.
- Nothing ever cleans that directory (`flutter clean` touches only `flutter_app/build/`; gym's `clean: true` cleans through the very `build.db` that corrupted), and up to three concurrent runner registrations share it (gh-2026).
- Run 43160591145 died 12 min into the archive on the corrupted-state trio — missing bridging PCH, missing `Runner_const_extract_protocols.json`, `build.db: disk I/O error` — while the **same tree built green the two previous days** (only delta was gh-2120, unrelated to iOS).

### Fix
- `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` (`ios build_only`): pin a workspace-local per-run dir (`build/ios/archive-dd`) as gym `derived_data_path`, pin `archive_path` next to it (the old default `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives/<date>/fa.xcarchive` is a shared same-day collision surface), and `FileUtils.rm_rf` it before archiving; the gh-160 checkout re-clones the workspace every run, so the path starts clean by construction.
- Isolation over purge: never `rm -rf` the shared per-user root — a sibling registration's archive may be live inside it (negative checks pin this).

### Test Coverage
- `test/workflow_ios_derived_data_guard_test.dart` — new workflow-shape guard, written first, **RED** against the old lane (4 failures), **GREEN** after the fix (AC1 workspace-local derived data, AC2 removal before archive, AC3 workspace-local archive, AC4 negatives: no shared-root purge).
- Sibling guards: `workflow_ios_archive_observability` / `workflow_ios_platform_download_guard` / `workflow_selfhosted_legs` / `release_ipa_strip` — 29 PASSED; all 8 `flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb` PASSED; `ruby -c Fastfile` OK.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **13780 passed, 13 skipped** (exit 0).

### Notes
- Legacy `Runner-*` DerivedData dirs remain on fa-m5-1/2/3 as dead weight; owner may reclaim disk (suspected contributor to the I/O error) via `rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData` **only while no iOS/macOS build runs on any registration**.
- Fresh derived data costs a few minutes per archive (gym already ran `clean: true`; the delta is module/PCH caches only).
- The macOS desktop lane (`build-macos.yml`) shares the per-user root and may hit the same class — out of scope for this ticket, flagged for follow-up.

## gh-2125 — [daily-publish] testflight leg failed: fixed

**Root cause**: The TestFlight leg's gym archive ran with no `-derivedDataPath`/`archive_path`, so `xcodebuild archive` used the **default per-user Xcode DerivedData** (`~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-ecmk…`) on the persistent self-hosted Mac — a directory nothing in the pipeline ever cleans, shared by up to three concurrent runner registrations (gh-2026). Run 43160591145 died 12 minutes into the archive on the corrupted-state trio (missing bridging PCH, missing `Runner_const_extract_protocols.json`, `build.db: disk I/O error`); the same tree built green the two prior days, proving runner state, not code.

**Fix** (commit `7df90c6` on `ai/gh-2125`): `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` `ios build_only` now pins a workspace-local per-run dir (`build/ios/archive-dd`) as gym `derived_data_path` and `archive_path`, and `FileUtils.rm_rf`s it before archiving — clean by construction since the gh-160 checkout re-clones the workspace every run. Isolation over purge: the shared per-user root is never blanket-deleted (a sibling registration's archive may be live inside it — pinned by negative checks).

**Fix** (commit `7df90c6` on `ai/gh-2125`): `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile` `ios build_only` now pins a workspace-local per-run dir (`build/ios/archive-dd`) as gym `derived_data_path` and `archive_path`, and `FileUtils.rm_rf`s it before archiving — clean by construction since the gh-160 checkout re-clones the workspace every run. Isolation over purge: the shared per-user root is never blanket-deleted (a sibling registration's archive may be live inside it — pinned by negative checks).
